cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD's. Moses says to arm some men "…that they may go against the Midianites and execute the LORD’s vengeance on them." (Numbers 31:3) The vengeance isn't Moses' idea. It comes from what the LORD told him in verse 2. So the army goes out as the ones carrying out the LORD's word, friends, and that's the whole point.

The answer is True! The text says they "…waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses…" (Numbers 31:7) Nobody is freelancing here, friends. The order came from the LORD, and the army carried it out the way it was given.

The answer is their herds, flocks and goods. Verse 9 says they "…plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods." (Numbers 31:9) The women and children were captured, and the animals and belongings were taken too. It was a big haul, bakers, and the numbers later in the chapter show just how big.

The answer is "burn." The text says they "…burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments…" (Numbers 31:10) Both the cities and the encampments went up. It's a heavy detail, friends, and the text gives it straight.

The answer is False. The army carried away "…all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals." (Numbers 31:11) And they brought "…the captives, spoils, and plunder…" to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation. (Numbers 31:12) The plunder came to the camp right along with the captives.

The answer is that Moses asks if they spared all the women. He says to the officers, "Have you spared all the women?" (Numbers 31:15) He's angry when he asks it, and the very next verse is where he explains himself. I think this is a heavy part of the story, friends, and it's worth reading slowly.

The answer is Balaam son of Beor. Moses says the women caused Israel to turn unfaithfully "…through the counsel of Balaam…" (Numbers 31:16) Balaam was already named among the slain in verse 8. Here Moses ties his name to what happened at Peor, bakers.

The answer is "congregation." The LORD says to "…divide the captives between the troops who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation." (Numbers 31:27) Two shares, one for the soldiers and one for everybody else. That's a clean split, friends, and the LORD is the one who laid it out.

The answer is False. The commanders say, "…not one of us is missing." (Numbers 31:49) They counted the soldiers under their command and reported nobody missing. Friends, I'd have counted twice and still been nervous.

The answer is to make atonement for themselves. The commanders say they brought the gold offering "…to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD." (Numbers 31:50) They gave armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings and necklaces. The text states the reason in their own words, bakers.

The answer is True. Verse 53 says it simply: "Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself." (Numbers 31:53) It's a short line, friends, but it tells you the soldiers kept something of their own. I think it's worth a pause that it sits right after all that gold for the LORD.

The answer is into the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Eleazar brought the gold "…into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD." (Numbers 31:54) The gold didn't get stashed in someone's tent, friends. It went to the Tent of Meeting, where it stood as a memorial.
